feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
entry.summary:
Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM) improves agent decisions by combining a frozen language model semantic encoder with a shared, frozen conditional predictor (LimiX-2) that infers task targets from deployment evidence without parameter updates.

Why it matters: By decoupling semantic representation from empirical inference, DPDM allows LLM agents to continuously learn from deployment history and improve decision accuracy without costly model fine-tuning.

entry.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
entry.summary:
VFlash introduces Flash Primitive Decoding, a method using a lightweight drafter to predict structured visual primitives jointly in a single forward pass instead of token-by-token.

Why it matters: By drastically reducing generation latency while improving spatial accuracy, VFlash enables real-time visual goal and trajectory planning for physical AI systems like robotics and autonomous driving.

entry.title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
entry.summary:
Harness-S uses a fixed pool of specialized sibling harnesses to rescue failed policy attempts during training, distilling auxiliary execution capabilities into a single policy that executes under the original base harness.

Why it matters: It allows AI agents to internalize capabilities discovered through diverse, specialized execution environments without requiring complex or non-standard harnesses at deployment time.

entry.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
entry.summary:
BestRand is a benchmark compression method that mitigates random sampling's high-error tail while cutting subset construction costs and improving out-of-distribution estimation accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables stable, accurate, and cheap LLM and multimodal evaluation by preventing the rare, massive estimation errors inherent to basic random sampling.

entry.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
entry.summary:
WeLM-Image is a unified image foundation model using a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with sparse Mixture-of-Experts to integrate multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, editing, and multi-reference synthesis.

Why it matters: It enables high-resolution image generation, instruction editing, and multi-reference synthesis within a single unified model efficient enough for single-GPU consumer deployments.

entry.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
entry.summary:
TailSteer is a final-stage training framework that prevents multi-turn visual drift by concentrating preservation corrections at the tail of on-policy denoising trajectories.

Why it matters: It allows foundation image models to sustain robust multi-turn editing over long horizons without requiring expensive retraining or specialized inference-time mechanisms.

entry.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
entry.summary:
SLA is a Spatial-Language-Action model that integrates implicit spatial alignment into continual pre-training for VLAs using 3D perception supervision without adding inference overhead.

Why it matters: It establishes transferable 3D spatial understanding as a foundational capability in vision-language-action models while maintaining zero additional computational cost during deployment.

entry.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
entry.summary:
EvoMemState is a state-centric long-term memory framework for LLM agents that augments persistent facts with evolving Relational States and a request-specific Reasoning State trained via reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It improves retrieval completeness and response accuracy in long-term personal AI agents by explicitly modeling how facts conflict, relate, and apply to specific user requests over time.

entry.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
D3D is a standalone diffusion drafter that decouples candidate generation from target-model hidden states, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding by drafting successor blocks concurrently during target verification.

Why it matters: By eliminating sequential dependencies between drafting and target verification, D3D significantly increases inference throughput for large language models without degrading acceptance performance.

entry.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
entry.summary:
Drex is a family of four open decision models (up to 27B parameters) that output probability distributions over user-provided options in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding.

Why it matters: Decision models like Drex dramatically reduce latency and inference costs while providing consistent, non-autoregressive output formats for structured classification and scoring tasks.

entry.title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
VisSearch-Bench introduces 204 human-written tasks across 5 search categories to evaluate multimodal agents on long-horizon visual search and visual context management.

Why it matters: Current multimodal models struggle significantly with tasks requiring long-horizon reasoning that bridges visual evidence, spatial relations, and web search retrieval.

entry.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
entry.summary:
Hybrid Computer Use (HCU) is a unified interface for general agents that combines programmatic, accessibility-based semantic, and visual GUI interactions to improve execution efficiency and accuracy.

Why it matters: Enabling agents to flexibly combine programmatic, semantic, and visual modalities reduces round-trip latency and overcomes the performance bottlenecks of purely visual, human-centric GUI interfaces.

entry.title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer
entry.summary:
PLatour is an open-source framework connecting frozen language models via zero-initialized linear bridges for Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer, paired with PACT-Check to verify genuine communication gains.

Why it matters: It provides tools to efficiently combine large and small language models while offering a critical diagnostic method to prevent false attribution of performance gains to latent cross-model communication.

entry.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
entry.summary:
Open-HumanScale provides an open-source recipe and 50,000-hour curated egocentric video corpus (Open-HumanScale-50K) for pretraining embodied world-action models.

Why it matters: It establishes a reproducible, open-source framework and empirical scaling law for leveraging massive egocentric human video to improve physical robot generalization.

entry.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
entry.summary:
Researchers derived SIMPLE, a four-parameter analytical law that predicts LLM inference energy consumption across model architectures and NVIDIA H100 GPUs without per-LLM calibration.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, uncalibrated prediction of LLM inference energy costs, uncovering energy inefficiencies in long-context, agentic, and extended reasoning workloads.

entry.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) that use a label-free RL objective to generate text exemplars directly from language model residual stream directions, bypassing the limitations of corpus search.

Why it matters: MAEMs offer a grounded, scalable approach to mechanistically interpret internal model representations without relying on fixed external text corpora or manual labeling.

entry.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
A new parallel decoding method for diffusion language models uses internal forward-pass probes to directly measure token coupling, improving decoding speed over standard mean-field decoding.

Why it matters: It enables faster inference and lower step counts for diffusion language models without requiring model retraining or architectural modifications.

entry.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics
entry.summary:
Researchers established an analytical framework using high-dimensional invariant boxes to prove that the first token acts as an exponential attractor in deep Mamba models, driving token clustering and attention-sink behavior.

Why it matters: Proving that Mamba architecture inherently exhibits first-token attraction provides a mathematical foundation for understanding attention-sink phenomena and token clustering in state-space models.

entry.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
entry.summary:
SpecCTMC is a training-free speculative sampler for masked diffusion language models that reduces sequential evaluations without a separate draft model while preserving the exact continuous-time Markov chain distribution.

Why it matters: It enables significantly faster parallel text generation in diffusion language models while maintaining exact output distribution fidelity without requiring retraining or auxiliary draft models.

entry.title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
entry.summary:
Hybrid State Transfer (HST) enables cross-model state handoff in hybrid linear-attention LLMs by mapping full-attention K/V caches, recurrent states, and convolution histories to bypass prefill during model switches.

Why it matters: HST eliminates the overhead of repeating prefill over long contexts when routing or cascading between different sizes of hybrid linear-attention LLMs.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
A mechanistic framework analyzes how on-policy distillation's feedback loop causes limited student responsiveness and generation degeneration, while showing offline distillation can successfully prepare models for effective on-policy training.

Why it matters: Understanding OPD's feedback mechanics helps practitioners avoid training degeneration and effectively sequence offline preparation to unlock downstream performance gains in post-training.

entry.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
CoRD improves on-policy distillation by generating rollout states from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher models using maximal coupling from speculative decoding.

Why it matters: CoRD provides a more data-efficient sampling mechanism that exposes student models to critical teacher states without needing frequent or ad-hoc state interventions.

entry.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
entry.summary:
Researchers mapped masked diffusion parallel text generation to statistical physics and random sequential adsorption, deriving an exact solution for Markov data and a thermodynamic metric to calculate optimal unmasking schedules.

Why it matters: The theoretical framework enables the mathematical optimization of unmasking schedules to improve speed and output quality in parallel-decoded masked diffusion models.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers established scaling laws for sparse autoencoder (SAE) training data, demonstrating that replaying a fixed activation buffer after reaching a quality plateau achieves performance equivalent to using entirely fresh activations.

Why it matters: This approach significantly reduces activation storage requirements by up to 64x during SAE training, dramatically lowering memory bottlenecks and compute costs without sacrificing model interpretability or reconstruction quality.

entry.title: O$^2$PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix
entry.summary:
Overlap-gated On-Policy Distillation (O²PD) restricts distillation to the first 20% prefix tokens of student rollouts and uses an overlap-gated α-divergence to address top-k alignment failure modes.

Why it matters: O²PD improves student model training efficiency and stability by filtering out unreliable off-policy teacher supervision and resolving support mismatches in top-k distillation.

entry.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
entry.summary:
NEO-VLA is an encoder-free vision-language-action framework that tokenizes images via patch convolutions, enabling a flow-matching action expert to access multi-depth visual representations.

Why it matters: Directly integrating visual feature computation into the action backbone provides better spatial details and increases control robustness across distribution shifts in robotic manipulation.

entry.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
entry.summary:
FrontierPhysics is a benchmark featuring 56 expert-authored end-to-end tasks across nine physics domains to evaluate whether AI agents can conduct correct, publishable research from literature review to manuscript generation.

Why it matters: It establishes an end-to-end evaluation framework that highlights critical reasoning and intuition bottlenecks in AI agents attempting autonomous scientific discovery.

entry.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
entry.summary:
A study evaluates multi-turn agentic RL using Pass@(K,T), revealing performance depends on turn budgets, primarily aids error recovery rather than single-step decisions, and introduces BudgetMix RL to improve resilience across execution settings.

Why it matters: Understanding RL's reliance on interaction depth allows developers to optimize training regimes like BudgetMix RL, ensuring agents remain effective under strict inference-time turn constraints.

entry.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
entry.summary:
PyRUA-DataFarm replaces human teleoperators with an LLM coding agent that builds simulation environments and expert controllers from one calibration episode, using a video model to render real-ready policy training data.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for manual robot teleoperation and physical hardware during data collection, lowering the cost and increasing the visual robustness of real-world policy deployment.

entry.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
entry.summary:
EmoReward introduces a self-evolving training mechanism for emotional video generation RL that uses reflective reward gating and historical reward traces to adaptively calibrate multi-reward fusion weights between training runs.

Why it matters: It mitigates reward hacking and subjective aesthetic inconsistencies in video RL post-training by dynamically weighting emotional cues without needing manual reward engineering or continuous reward model fine-tuning.

entry.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
entry.summary:
StreamDuo pairs a trainable streaming commentator with a frozen research agent that retrieves game wiki entries in real-time to enable accurate commentary on unseen games.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a viable framework for streaming video LLMs to zero-shot adapt to novel visual domains without unlearning general timing or hallucinating domain-specific terminology.

entry.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
entry.summary:
Solv3R is a looped transformer architecture that uses an iteration-independent update operator to iteratively refine multi-view geometry estimates and integrate new image observations.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for separate task-specific models in 3D reconstruction by enabling scalable, iterative refinement and real-time frame streaming within a single transformer framework.

entry.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
entry.summary:
H2RB is a co-training framework that adapts pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies using unpaired human and robot demonstrations by bridging representation and action spaces.

Why it matters: H2RB enables scalable policy adaptation by leveraging easy-to-collect human demonstrations, significantly reducing the reliance on expensive target-robot data collection.

entry.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
entry.summary:
Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD) unifies score and flow matching via a learned critic, enabling VA-TDM to achieve state-of-the-art four-step image and video generation.

Why it matters: VA-TDM enables high-fidelity, few-step image and video generation on massive models, significantly reducing computational inference costs while retaining full-model quality.

entry.title: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?
entry.summary:
VideoMemBench evaluates in-context video memory in MLLMs using multi-turn dialogues with cross-turn dependencies requiring models to recall prior visual contexts and their own past answers.

Why it matters: Current MLLMs fail to maintain context across multi-turn video conversations, highlighting a major limitation in deploying models for continuous interactive video analysis.

entry.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
entry.summary:
TAC-CoT is an adaptive implicit Chain-of-Thought framework that replaces explicit reasoning text with compact latent tokens while preserving textual tokens for tool calls, observations, and final answers.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to execute tool-assisted reasoning with significantly lower generation overhead without sacrificing accuracy or tool-use capabilities.

entry.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Muon-RT eliminates Muon's separate momentum buffer during self-distillation by reusing the teacher-student model displacement to compute orthogonalized update vectors with reduced training memory.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces persistent GPU memory overhead during LLM self-distillation while simultaneously outperforming both AdamW and standard Muon in model accuracy.

entry.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
SpecOPD accelerates speculative decoding drafter training using branch-parallel on-policy distillation, decoupling supervision from sequential rollouts while optimizing acceptance length directly via an E2E-TV surrogate.

Why it matters: It dramatically scales up on-policy distillation efficiency for speculative decoding drafters, yielding significant inference speedups across diverse model architectures up to 125B parameters.

entry.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
LoopVQ introduces a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that jointly codes multi-loop step channels and fine-tunes codebooks, achieving sub 1-bit quantization.

Why it matters: It eliminates the primary memory bottleneck in parameter-efficient looped transformers, enabling massive throughput gains and lower latency for long-context inference.

entry.title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
entry.summary:
PyRUA-REAL is a framework for embodied recursive self-improvement that enables coding agents to transform real-world robot exploration into persistent memory and reusable executable code skills.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a method for robots to continuously improve their capabilities through physical interaction and convert that experience into efficient, reusable autonomous code.

entry.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
entry.summary:
Coca-Cola compresses LLM agent tool observations into continuous latent tokens instead of raw text, using Action-Preserving Training to maintain decision-critical information while drastically cutting context size and latency.

Why it matters: By bypassing text-based tool outputs in favor of continuous latent embeddings, multi-step LLM agents can run significantly faster and cheaper without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks
entry.summary:
A 36-expert study shows that model merging does not require uniform LoRA ranks across experts, provided the merge method avoids selecting spectral components purely by magnitude.

Why it matters: Practitioners can independently optimize the LoRA rank for each domain expert without degrading model performance during post-hoc merging.

entry.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
D3D introduces a standalone diffusion drafter combining blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding without waiting for target-model hidden states.

Why it matters: Eliminating the dependency on target-model hidden states allows overlapping execution of drafting and verification phases, significantly accelerating LLM inference speed.

entry.title: EvoOPD: Evolving Privileged Information Strategies for Black-Box On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
EvoOPD optimizes black-box language model distillation by dynamically evolving privileged information (PI) feedback strategies from the teacher based on the student model's changing state.

Why it matters: It enables effective fine-grained distillation from proprietary, logit-inaccessible language models by dynamically matching teacher feedback to the student's evolving learning needs.

entry.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
entry.summary:
Prompting LLMs with specific political personas systematically alters their latent space representational geometry, reorganizing word projections and semantic axis alignments.

Why it matters: Context-dependent reorganization of latent representations can undermine the reliability of standard LLM feature monitoring and safety evaluation tools like linear probes and sparse autoencoders.

entry.title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models
entry.summary:
LooM introduces a causal encoder-decoder architecture that loops decoder layers using a loop-invariant key-value cache, enabling flexible dynamic depth without increasing memory usage.

Why it matters: LooM allows deployment-time compute scaling up to 21 layer executions per token without increasing memory footprint or requiring structural model changes.

entry.title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse
entry.summary:
A study on non-prefix KV-cache reuse demonstrates that allocating a 5% repair budget to recomputing target chunks against reused context yields higher accuracy than re-inserting original prefill KV tensors or using InfoFlow reordering.

Why it matters: It establishes that limited computational repair budgets are best spent recomputing target chunks in place rather than restoring original prefill KV states or reordering context.

entry.title: Does Context Compression Preserve Refusal Alignment?
entry.summary:
Encoder-based context compression systematically weakens refusal alignment in instruction-tuned language models by attenuating activations along the decoder's refusal direction, despite high semantic reconstruction fidelity.

Why it matters: Systems using compressed context representations to save inference costs risk exposing safety vulnerabilities unless alignment-relevant features are explicitly preserved.

entry.title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
entry.summary:
Researchers developed an automated pipeline that combined LLM judges with evolutionary, RL, and subliminal learning methods to generate a dataset of 6,575 training datasets with surprising side effects across eight model behaviors.

Why it matters: Automating the discovery of unexpected training side effects provides a benchmark to study out-of-domain generalization and predict model misbehaviors prior to deployment.

entry.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
entry.summary:
FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark comprising 56 expert-authored tasks designed to evaluate AI agents across complete physics research workflows.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous evaluation standard that shifts AI physics benchmarks from solving isolated static problems to assessing full-lifecycle research competence.

entry.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
entry.summary:
Route Anything is a unified framework and theoretical foundation for dynamic, omni-modal model and policy routing across heterogeneous candidate models to balance performance and computational cost.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that orchestrating specialized AI models via learned routers yields superior performance across modalities while substantially reducing compute costs compared to single fixed models.

entry.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
entry.summary:
LoCo introduces local preference learning for reasoning compression by training models on state-conditioned preference pairs via DPO to detect when to stop overthinking and conclude reasoning.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers inference costs by cutting reasoning length while preserving task accuracy and generalizing across domains without domain-specific retraining.

entry.title: Words Caught in the Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression for Self-Opaque Clients in Psychotherapy
entry.summary:
Pandora is a psychotherapy client simulation framework that uses explicit expression planning and distilled linguistic patterns to model self-opaque client responses accurately.

Why it matters: Explicit expression planning improves the realism of AI client simulators by aligning responses with individual speech patterns and avoiding premature, overly clear explanations of distress.

entry.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
entry.summary:
Insights from the Kling video generation pipeline show that generation quality depends on a unified multimodal understanding chain spanning Kling-MLLM, specialized captioning, agentic prompt enhancement, perceptual text encoder training, and localized reward modeling.

Why it matters: It provides a blueprint for shifting video generation control from simple rendering to deep semantic control by optimizing the underlying multimodal understanding stack.

entry.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
entry.summary:
DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model to extract compact, disentangled latent action representations that serve as a shared interface across human and robot embodiments.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified latent action space that enables cross-embodiment policy transfer and lowers the computational cost of video-diffusion-based robot control.

entry.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
entry.summary:
Axion 1.0 is an open agent foundation model trained using a simplified, three-stage recipe comprising two lightweight SFT stages and reinforcement learning, omitting mid-training, DPO, and on-policy distillation.

Why it matters: It proves that competitive, broad agentic capabilities can be achieved using a streamlined training process, while providing the open-source community with a fully reproducible pipeline.

entry.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
entry.summary:
FactEmbed decouples compositional query comprehension in MLLMs by using factorized latents and an intermediate target imagination objective to improve Composed Image Retrieval (CIR).

Why it matters: It improves CIR retrieval accuracy by forcing MLLMs to ground visual modifications explicitly rather than relying solely on direct contrastive embedding mapping.

entry.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
ToolSpace introduces a tool-centric environment synthesis framework that constructs task environments by mining dependencies from real Model Context Protocol execution traces rather than relying on LLM judgments.

Why it matters: By relying on execution-grounded tool dependencies rather than LLM assertions, ToolSpace creates harder, highly realistic long-horizon benchmarks and significantly improves open agent model capabilities.

entry.title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
entry.summary:
YANAMI introduces a large-scale dataset (YANAMI-400K) and benchmark (YANAMI-Bench) designed to train and evaluate Unified Multimodal Models on multiturn stateful interactions requiring continuous tracking of evolving visual dialogue states.

Why it matters: It addresses the limitations of single-turn and stateless datasets by providing the supervision and evaluation metrics needed to build models capable of complex, turn-by-turn image generation and editing.

entry.title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
entry.summary:
VidUEU-Agent is an automated pipeline that synthesizes multimodal instruction data from raw videos using an autonomous, training-feedback-driven four-stage framework.

Why it matters: It reduces reliance on expensive human annotations by enabling models to self-improve through automated, feedback-guided video instruction dataset curation.

entry.title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
entry.summary:
EvoTeam is a framework that jointly evolves team organization, team-specific interaction rules, and reusable individual agent skills using execution experience to improve multi-agent collaboration across heterogeneous tasks.

Why it matters: It prevents performance degradation in multi-agent systems by ensuring that collaboration strategies and team structures evolve alongside individual agent capabilities rather than relying on static, shared interaction rules.

entry.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
entry.summary:
WebHarbor is a open-source suite of 153 dockerized, executable website environments containing 3,518 tasks for deterministic evaluation and reinforcement learning training of GUI web agents.

Why it matters: It solves the reproducibility and stability issues of live website benchmarking while offering realistic, functional environments for training generalizable GUI agents via reinforcement learning.

entry.title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
entry.summary:
Caper is a consequence-aware approval mechanism for autonomous coding agents that pre-executes shell commands in a snapshotted sandbox to evaluate their actual effects before committing or rolling them back.

Why it matters: Evaluating actual execution consequences in a sandbox prevents harmful side effects hidden deep within invoked scripts and workspace states before they impact the main environment.

entry.title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
entry.summary:
Mage-VL-Cowork is a 4B hybrid computer-use agent trained via a five-stage curriculum using synthesized tasks to reach 66.0% accuracy on OSWorld-Verified.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that small 4B models can achieve state-of-the-art hybrid computer interaction performance using scalable task synthesis and harness evolution, advancing efficient on-device automation.

entry.title: MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery
entry.summary:
MoLRSI is a recursive self-improving AI agent that optimizes molecular discovery workflows and model architectures using persistent cross-task memory to enhance its search policy over time.

Why it matters: The system demonstrates that self-improving AI agents can autonomously optimize complex biological workflows to outperform expert-designed protocols and generic scientific AI models in real-world molecular and peptide discovery.

entry.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
entry.summary:
An independent empirical study shows Direct Nash Optimization (DNO-Prct) boosts open-weight LLM win rates on AlpacaEval 2.0, maintaining most gains even when using open-weight annotators instead of GPT-4o.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that Direct Nash Optimization can significantly improve open-weight model alignment without relying on proprietary models like GPT-4o for preference ratings.

entry.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce PEARL, a GRPO variant that suppresses misaligned language model behaviors durably by augmenting rollouts with continuations from cached intermediate trajectory states.

Why it matters: It provides a mechanism to permanently remove harmful language model behaviors without them re-emerging during downstream fine-tuning or degrading general capabilities.

entry.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
Adversarial Speculative Reasoning trains draft models to be rejected at critical decision points, forcing the target model to directly sample high-precision tokens and improve long-horizon agent accuracy.

Why it matters: It reframes speculative decoding from a passive speed accelerator into an active context-precision allocator that boosts agent performance without modifying or retraining the underlying target model.

entry.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
LoopVQ reduces looped transformer memory bottlenecks by jointly vector-quantizing key-value cache channels across redundant loop steps, achieving sub 1-bit compression while maintaining high task accuracy.

Why it matters: It eliminates the primary memory bottleneck of parameter-efficient looped transformers, enabling massive throughput gains and lower latency during long-context and chain-of-thought inference.

entry.title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
entry.summary:
Fine-tuning LLMs on benign data they perceive as false induces broad misalignment, driven by internal inconsistency between generated outputs and internal probability distributions.

Why it matters: Updating LLM knowledge with benign-looking data can accidentally degrade safety alignment if the model fails to internalize the new facts as true.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve
entry.summary:
A study evaluating language-subspace interventions across four LLMs reveals that projecting out estimated language subspaces fails to eliminate language information and frequently sacrifices target language fidelity to achieve accuracy gains.

Why it matters: Evaluating language-subspace interventions strictly on task accuracy masks performance trade-offs, showing that current projection methods fail to cleanly isolate language representations without degrading target language output.

entry.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
entry.summary:
A new framework evaluates LLM knowledge retention and unlearning robustness by measuring the geometric fragmentation and entropy of anon-vectors across hidden state layers.

Why it matters: It enables direct, single-phase measurement of suppressed knowledge and unlearning security at the representation layer without relying on easily bypassed behavioral outputs or computationally expensive adversarial attacks.

entry.title: Going Deeper With Memories
entry.summary:
DeepMem is a causal multiscale byte-level architecture that uses an invertible subband transform, fast weight memory blocks, and an attention-based super-resolution decoder to separate semantic compression from exact byte preservation.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, tokenizer-free byte-level language modeling by processing compressed semantic representations at a fraction of the computational cost while maintaining exact byte reconstruction.

entry.title: ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals
entry.summary:
ARLoop introduces a looped transformer architecture using sliding-window depth attention residuals to selectively aggregate intermediate representations across recurrent steps instead of relying on standard residual streams.

Why it matters: ARLoop provides a parameter-efficient scaling mechanism that enhances model performance on math and coding tasks without increasing physical layer counts or token consumption.

entry.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
entry.summary:
LoCo is a local preference learning method that compresses reasoning trajectories by using state-conditioned DPO to train models on when to stop deliberating.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces LLM inference costs and latency for reasoning tasks without sacrificing model performance.

entry.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
entry.summary:
Wave Forcing co-designs model architecture, training, and execution to enable continuous, multi-step video generation at 134.8 end-to-end FPS using a 1F1C pipeline.

Why it matters: It eliminates the serial bottleneck of autoregressive video generation, enabling real-time, low-latency streaming of high-quality long videos.

entry.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
entry.summary:
CoworkOS is a general-purpose harness for long-horizon agent work that decouples task strategy from execution management via a three-layer architecture, shared application layer, and persistent semantic memory.

Why it matters: It enables continuous, long-horizon human-agent collaboration and real-world task execution without losing state, context, or revision history during complex workflows.

entry.title: Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics
entry.summary:
Researchers present a unified taxonomy for agentic computer graphics alongside an agentic literature system designed to automatically analyze paper developments at scale.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured framework to categorize and systematically analyze the rapid rise of LLM-based agents that generate and iteratively refine graphics code.

entry.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
This paper analyzes the intersection of video generation and world modeling using an executable agent harness to coordinate multi-shot generation, world state execution, and recursive self-improvement.

Why it matters: Structuring video models around an executable agent harness enables programmatic control, interactive world simulation, and continuous self-improvement beyond simple end-to-end prompt synthesis.

entry.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
entry.summary:
CUA-Master introduces a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework using open-world seeding, trajectory reconstruction, and snapshot-rollback execution to continuously scale computer-use agents.

Why it matters: The framework overcomes the diminishing returns of self-generated agent experience by enabling continuous, reliable open-world data synthesis across GUI and CLI environments.

entry.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced uni-robot-agent, an open-weight unified harness for Robot-Use Agents that enables training and achieves competitive manipulation performance without privileged inputs.

Why it matters: It removes reliance on proprietary foundation models by offering an open framework that matches or exceeds closed-source performance on robotics tasks.

entry.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
entry.summary:
NorthCUA introduces a scalable computer-use agent framework using an Experience Flywheel, recursive self-improvement, staged supervised fine-tuning, and joint desktop-web reinforcement learning to achieve state-of-the-art open-source GUI performance.

Why it matters: NorthCUA provides an open-source model family and reusable architecture capable of executing long-horizon, complex software tasks across both desktop and web interfaces.

entry.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
entry.summary:
Reviso is an agentic video captioning framework that uses priority-guided active perception to selectively inspect temporal segments based on a hierarchical Context-Focus-Points observation plan.

Why it matters: By prioritizing essential visual evidence over minor details, Reviso improves overall video caption quality and enhances performance on downstream video question-answering tasks.

entry.title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
entry.summary:
PhotoGuider is a novel measure-then-frame method for 2D image cropping and 360° panorama framing that uses compact learned scorers over four structured photographic tokens and generates measurement-conditioned MLLM explanations.

Why it matters: PhotoGuider unifies camera parameter generation, 360° view framing, and 2D cropping into a single feature framework that provides explainable photographic assessments.

entry.title: SWE-Trail: History-Guided Trajectory Collection for Coding Agent Training
entry.summary:
SWE-Trail uses earlier sampling trajectories to direct subsequent collection efforts without exposing that history to the coding agent's context, preventing train-test mismatch during post-training.

Why it matters: It enables higher-quality trajectory data collection for training coding agents without causing models to depend on external advice or history that is absent at test time.

entry.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
entry.summary:
This paper presents a cross-cutting survey framework that unifies fragmented modality-specific embedding research into three capability tiers (coverage, comparability, compositionality) and three unification paths ending in joint embedding.

Why it matters: It offers a unified roadmap for AI researchers to transition from isolated, single-modality models to compositional, omnimodal embedding systems.

entry.title: CrossSWE: Benchmarking Cross-Repository Joint Development for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
CrossSWE is a new software engineering benchmark containing 171 instances across 165 repositories to evaluate coding agents on multi-repository joint development and change propagation.

Why it matters: It shifts AI coding benchmarks toward real-world software architecture challenges where agents must reason about cross-repository dependencies and maintain interface consistency.

entry.title: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?
entry.summary:
A new framework evaluates video world models, demonstrating that latent prediction error fails to reliably measure physical surprise despite representations encoding some physical information.

Why it matters: Researchers cannot rely on raw prediction error from video world models as a surrogate for physical surprise or causal understanding without confounding visual and static artifacts.

entry.title: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
entry.summary:
Avatar Intelligence introduces a paradigm for persistent personal agents that sustain long-term decision delegation, evaluated via the new Agentic Oversight Index.

Why it matters: It shifts personal AI evaluation toward measuring how effectively agents reduce routine human supervision while maintaining user control over consequential choices.

entry.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers identify the 'reference gap'—a failure to bind text to visual entities—as a key bottleneck in multimodal reasoning and introduce ReGap-Bench to evaluate visual scaffolding solutions.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that multimodal LLM performance can be significantly boosted without retraining by using task-matched visual scaffolding to ground language in image regions.

entry.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
entry.summary:
Sonar-MoE applies optimizer-in-backward updates to batched MoE expert tensors, freeing expert gradients immediately to reduce peak GPU memory without sacrificing step time or model accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables memory-efficient fine-tuning and scaling of large MoE models without incurring the severe execution speed penalties typical of per-expert updates.

entry.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
entry.summary:
Library of Layers (LoL) is a transformer architecture that dynamically orders its global pool of layers at runtime to adaptively compose computational graphs for specific tasks.

Why it matters: LoL enables runtime-configurable computational graphs, providing a single framework to optimize parameter efficiency, FLOP efficiency, and model safety control.

entry.title: Online Label-Free Gradient Matching for Continual Language Model Training
entry.summary:
OLGA is an online, label-free gradient matching method that distills streaming unlabeled text data using self-generated next-token targets to enable efficient continual language model training.

Why it matters: It enables continual language model updating on streaming, unlabeled data without full retraining, significantly lowering compute runtime while reducing catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
entry.summary:
Axion 1.0 is a fully open agent foundation model achieving competitive benchmark performance using a simplified three-stage training recipe without mid-training, DPO, or on-policy distillation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive agent foundation models can be developed with a simplified, fully reproducible training pipeline without complex intermediate optimization stages.

entry.title: Written Once, Read Differently How Language Models Own Answers Steer Their Next Ones
entry.summary:
A study of 22 open-weight LLMs reveals that self-commitment across sequential questions is mediated by a shared linear residual stream direction, but how models read this direction varies significantly across scale, instruction tuning, and prompts.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that models write consistent vector representations but read them unpredictably highlights a key mechanism and failure mode of internal consistency during multi-turn LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
entry.summary:
Researchers discovered that while Muon beats AdamW during pretraining, AdamW yields superior post-fine-tuning performance when pretraining data budgets are sufficiently large or as model size increases.

Why it matters: Choosing an optimizer purely based on pretraining loss efficiency can lead to suboptimal downstream performance after fine-tuning at large data and model scales.

entry.title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
entry.summary:
RLVR can cause models to switch from structured derivations to ineffective brute-force enumeration under out-of-distribution shifts, a failure mitigated by co-training on bijective inversion tasks without requiring process supervision.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high in-distribution accuracy in RLVR does not guarantee strategy generalization, but simple co-training interventions can implicitly enforce robust reasoning under OOD shifts without process-level rewards.

entry.title: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
entry.summary:
FADE improves RLVR efficiency via a bilinear state-space filter that separates fast-changing policy ability from slow-changing prompt difficulty to target informative rollouts.

Why it matters: FADE optimizes the allocation of generation budgets in RLVR by preventing zero-advantage rollouts without relying on stale or noisy prompt pass-rate trackers.

entry.title: A Scaling Theory of Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Time Overfitting and Ensembling
entry.summary:
Researchers established a scaling theory for multi-epoch pretraining using logit-averaged ensembles, using dynamical mean-field theory to prove ensembling mitigates late-time overfitting and shifts optimal compute-allocation laws.

Why it matters: As pretraining becomes data-constrained rather than compute-constrained, training multi-model ensembles over multiple epochs offers a compute-efficient path to lower test loss without requiring new tokens.

entry.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
entry.summary:
FLAMIA introduces attention kernels optimized for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs that use MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 precision to achieve safe, consistent, and up to 1.42x faster training.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how to effectively translate low-precision hardware capabilities on Blackwell GPUs into end-to-end training acceleration for long-context Transformer models without compromising quality.
